videos.title: 30.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
30.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

The Panthers have won three straight and six of their past eight.

videos.summary_source_text:
Keep the Belt Ahead of the Buttons  #golfswing #golftips A great way to avoid reverse spine angle and improve your body motion is to make sure the belt stays ahead of the buttons throughout the swing. When the chest outraces the lower body, the upper body tilts the wrong way and creates poor rotation patterns. Leading with the belt keeps your hips and torso sequencing correctly, helping you stay in posture and rotate more efficiently. This simple cue creates a better backswing, a cleaner transition, and a more stable downswing.

videos.title: EVERY Shot | Wyndham Clark relives frustrating round at VidantaWorld Mexico Open
videos.summary_source_text:
EVERY Shot | Wyndham Clark relives frustrating round at VidantaWorld Mexico Open Sometimes, golf is hard. Go all-access with two-time major champion Wyndham Clark as he breaks down every shot from his first-round 69 at the 2026 VidantaWorld Mexico Only. Despite ranking 6th on approach and 9th of the tee, Clark lost 4.85 strokes on the greens on Thursday. 

The PGA Tour heads to Vidanta Vallarta for the VidantaWorld Mexico Open, the fifth event of the FedExCup Fall, with crucial points up for grabs. Wyndham Clark headlines the field after a three-win season, while Tom Kim returns following his Asian Games gold medal and Brian Campbell looks to become the tournament’s first back-to-back winner. Ben Griffin, Blades Brown and past champion Tony Finau add further quality, with Aldrich Potgieter back after losing a playoff to Campbell last year. With several players battling around the FedExCup top-100 bubble, the stakes are high in Mexico as the season approaches its conclusion.

videos.summary_source_text:
Your Feet May Be Warning You About Your Health—Look for These Signs | Dr. Mandell Your feet may be warning you about serious health problems before you even realize something is wrong! In this eye-opening video, Dr. Alan Mandell reveals 7 important warning signs in your feet that could provide clues about poor circulation, diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, nerve damage, heart problems, kidney disease, and nutritional deficiencies. Discover what cold feet, burning or tingling toes, swollen ankles, changes in skin color, slow-healing wounds, unusual toenails, and pain while walking may be telling you about your body. Learn the fascinating physiology behind these symptoms, how your blood vessels and nerves affect your feet, and why recognizing certain changes early can help protect your long-term health. Some of these symptoms have harmless explanations, while others deserve medical attention. Your feet carry you through life, but they can also reveal valuable clues about your overall well-being. Don't ignore what your body may be telling you! Watch until the end to learn a simple 30-second foot check you can do at home. Share this important information with your family and friends, especially those living with diabetes or circulation problems. videos.title: Grok 4.8 Is Coming: Elon Musk’s 2.5 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.8 Is Coming: Elon Musk’s 2.5 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCGIiO6Uo8V8vkuLOcFvf3ZQ/join

Elon Musk just revealed Grok 4.8, a massive 2.5-trillion-parameter AI model built on xAI's completely rewritten C++ training stack. But here's the twist: Musk isn't claiming Grok 4.8 will beat GPT-6 Astra or Claude Fable. He's saving that prediction for Grok 4.9.

So what's the real purpose of Grok 4.8? And why could its speed matter more than its intelligence?

According to Musk, Grok 4.8 has 2.5 trillion parameters, compared with 2.1 trillion for Grok 4.7 and 1.5 trillion for Grok 4.6. That's a 19% increase over its predecessor. But bigger models don't automatically mean better performance.

When Grok 4.7 launched on September 21, Artificial Analysis scored it at 46 on its Intelligence Index, just two points above Grok 4.6's score of 44. Despite a roughly 40% parameter increase, the overall improvement was relatively modest.

Grok 4.7 reportedly consumed approximately 81,000 output tokens per benchmark task, compared with around 27,000 for GPT-6 Astra. That's roughly three times the output tokens to complete the same evaluation.

For developers paying per token, that difference matters.

But Grok 4.8 introduces something potentially more important than another parameter increase: xAI's new C++ software stack.

Musk says the company has been rewriting its training and inference infrastructure to run closer to Nvidia's GB300 hardware, removing software layers that can slow down AI workloads.

He previously predicted that the new inference system could at least double performance for an earlier Grok model.

If those improvements materialize, Grok 4.8 could become a major test of whether xAI can make its increasingly massive models faster and cheaper to operate.

And there's another clue.

A September 28 commit in the open-source Magpie project revealed three Grok 4.8 configurations appearing in Cursor's model list:

grok-4.8-high
grok-4.8-high-fast
grok-4.8-xhigh-fast

These developer-facing identifiers suggest xAI is preparing multiple reasoning and speed configurations, although they don't confirm a release date or final capabilities.

Then, on October 7, Musk said that simple requests to the Grok bot on X would eventually be handled by a "lightning-fast" version of Grok 4.8.

That changes how we should think about this release.

Instead of competing exclusively for the highest AI benchmark scores, xAI may be preparing a model family optimized for different workloads: demanding coding and reasoning tasks on one side, and high-volume everyday requests on the other.

Meanwhile, the competition isn't standing still.

OpenAI has GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and the newly released GPT-6.1 Terra. Anthropic has Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. Google has entered the latest frontier-model competition with Gemini 4 Argon.

And GPT-6.1 Terra presents an especially interesting challenge.

At $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, Terra already undercuts Grok 4.7's $2 input and $6 output pricing. OpenAI also claims Terra completes tasks more than three times faster than Astra or Sol.

That means Grok 4.8 faces two very different battles.

Its most capable configurations need to close the intelligence gap with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

Its fast configurations need to prove they can compete on latency, efficiency, and cost.

But there are still major unknowns.

xAI hasn't officially announced Grok 4.8's release date, pricing, context window, architecture, or independent benchmark results. We also don't know whether its 2.5 trillion parameters represent the entire model or the parameters active during inference.

And there's no independent confirmation that the C++ rewrite delivers Musk's promised performance improvements.

This video breaks down what Musk actually confirmed, what the leaked Cursor configurations reveal, how Grok 4.8 compares with its biggest competitors, and why its most important achievement might have nothing to do with becoming the smartest AI model.

The real question isn't whether Grok 4.8 is bigger.

It's whether xAI can finally turn that scale into meaningful intelligence gains without paying an enormous price in speed and efficiency.

Would you rather have a smarter Grok 4.8 or a dramatically faster and cheaper one? Let us know in the comments.

Subscribe to BitBiased for independent AI analysis, model benchmarks, and the latest developments from OpenAI, xAI, Anthropic, and Google.

Paul Maurice, Panthers Morning Skate: Game v Jets, Hometown Remix Gear, Halloween Plans Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice speaks to the media in Fort Lauderdale before his team plays host to the Winnipeg Jets on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026.

On Thursday, Maurice updated the injury status of Sasha Barkov, Brad Marchand, and Jacob Markstrom.

Friday, he talked about the matchup with a Jets team that has lost seven straight, his plans for Halloween, what he will wear when the Panthers break out their pink Hometown Remix gear Monday, and more.

Florida has won two straight after beating the host Jets 5-1 on Tuesday. 

The Panthers took a 3-0 lead into the second off a pair of power-play goals from Carter Verhaeghe and one from Niko Mikkola. 

Florida had five players with multi-point games including Matthew Tkachuk (four assists), Seth Jones (three assists), and Brady Tkachuk (goal, two assists).

FREE TRAINING: https://train2point0.com/free-training

The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing, or "trying harder." videos.title: 29.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
29.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 29.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
Paul Maurice Updates Florida Panthers Injury Status of Barkov, Marchand, Markstrom Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice speaks to the media in Fort Lauderdale on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026.

Maurice updated the injury status of Sasha Barkov, Brad Marchand, and Jacob Markstrom.

🚨 Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is here, and its AI benchmark results are turning heads! But did Google really just beat ChatGPT, Claude, and every other AI model? Or is there a major catch behind the headlines?

Google DeepMind has announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a powerful new AI model designed for advanced cybersecurity, coding, vulnerability detection, and long-running autonomous AI tasks.

According to Google's reported results, Gemini 4 Carbon achieved an impressive 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 71.0% on CWE-bench, and a score of 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it ahead of several major AI competitors in the reported comparisons.

But here's the catch: Gemini 4 Carbon isn't publicly available, and its biggest performance claims haven't yet been independently verified.

In this Bitbiased AI breakdown, we examine Google's latest AI announcement, compare Gemini 4 Carbon against GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini 4 Argon, and reveal what the benchmarks actually tell us.

Is Gemini 4 Carbon really the smartest AI in the world? Let's find out.

🔥 WHAT YOU'LL DISCOVER IN THIS VIDEO:
✅ What Google DeepMind officially announced about Gemini 4 Carbon.

✅ How Google's new AI detects, exploits, and fixes software vulnerabilities.
✅ Why Google claims Gemini 4 Carbon can work autonomously for days.
✅ Why Gemini 4 Carbon is restricted to selected cybersecurity defenders.
✅ What its AI safety and prompt injection test results really mean.
✅ Why some of Google's biggest AI claims still need independent verification.
✅ Whether Gemini 4 Carbon deserves the title of the world's most powerful AI.

📊 GEMINI 4 CARBON BENCHMARK RESULTS
Google's reported cybersecurity performance:
🔹 SEC-bench Pro: 88.2% — Vulnerability discovery
🔹 ExploitGym: 54.8% — Exploit generation
🔹 CWE-bench: 71.0% — Vulnerability patching

Reported Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index scores:

🥇 Gemini 4 Carbon: 59
🥈 Claude Opus 5.5: 58
🥉 GPT-6 Astra: 57
🔹 Gemini 4 Argon: 50

These figures suggest that Gemini 4 Carbon is a serious contender among advanced AI models. However, a narrow lead on a composite benchmark doesn't automatically make it the best AI for every task.

The AI race between Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic is becoming more competitive than ever.

Google's Gemini 4 Carbon promises major improvements in cybersecurity, AI coding agents, vulnerability detection, software engineering, and long-horizon reasoning.

But can it really outperform ChatGPT and Claude?

In this video, we examine the evidence behind Google's claims, explain the differences between benchmark scores and real-world performance, and explore why limited public access makes independent verification difficult.

🔐 WHY IS GEMINI 4 CARBON RESTRICTED?

Unlike widely available AI models, Gemini 4 Carbon is initially being offered to selected cybersecurity defenders through Google's Fairwind Program.

Its ability to identify vulnerabilities and generate working exploits creates both defensive opportunities and potential security risks.

Google says it plans to expand access gradually, but a general public release date has not been announced.

videos.summary_source_text:
Älg och 28 år gammalt vin | #347 I Kapten Mat Äntligen blir det helstekt älgentrecôte med trattkantarellsås och mini-Pommes Anna på stekhällen. 
Kantarellsås till 4 personer, för stekhäll
• 250 g kantareller
• 1 schalottenlök, finhackad
• 1 vitlöksklyfta, finhackad
• 2 msk smör
• 5 enbär, krossade
• 3–5 dl viltfond (2 msk konc. viltfond)
• 3 dl vispgrädde
• Ev. 1 tsk soja 
• 1 tsk svartvinbärsgelé
• Salt & peppar

Gör så här
1. Rensa svampen och dela de stora.
2. Stek svampen torrt på en het del av hällen tills vätskan har kokat bort, ca 4 minuter.
3. Tillsätt smör, lök, vitlök, enbär och stek ca 3 minuter. 
4. Tillsätt fond och grädde och låt sjuda försiktigt i några minuter. Späd med vatten om såsen blir för tjock.
5. Smaka av med ev. soja, vinbärsgelé samt salt och peppar.

videos.summary_source_text:
The BEST Round Of Golf I've EVER Seen?! Is this the best round of golf ever? Join me as a play night golf in Portugal and find out if golf lessons can really turn an average golfer into a record-breaking player? Just how much can a 10 handicap golfer improve with the right golf instruction, better wedge play and smarter course management?

In this video, Mark Crossfield puts his golf coaching to the ultimate test as one of his students attempts to produce an extraordinary round of golf under the lights.

After working on his golf swing, wedge technique, distance control and approach shots, it's time to find out whether those improvements can translate into lower scores on the golf course.

What follows is one of the most unbelievable rounds of golf Mark has ever witnessed, with incredible wedge shots, outstanding short game performance and some seriously impressive scoring.

But can an everyday amateur golfer really challenge a course record?

Throughout the round, Mark explores the golf lessons and techniques that can help amateur golfers improve their ball striking, develop better distance control from 100 yards and in, hit more accurate wedge shots and ultimately shoot lower golf scores.

If you're a mid-handicap golfer looking to improve your golf game, sharpen your short game or discover how to score better without completely rebuilding your golf swing, there's plenty to learn from this extraordinary night golf challenge.

Can great golf coaching really make this much difference? Watch to find out!

videos.summary_source_text:
90 days of speed training starts today…. Every year I spend 3 months on speed training. I don’t want to get slower by age. Don’t let laziness kill your swing speed. Starting point this year was better than last year. Nice to see att 55 years old.

#golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro - Learn the curve before we change the swing path
1:00 It is good to start with a hook

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are misleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

I will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly.

I gave my Kimi AI trading bot access to a $10,000 trading account and 22 hours to trade with real money—but I didn't give it a ready-made trading strategy.

Could Kimi K3.1 make its own trading decisions, manage positions and finish profitably?

While it was trading, I gave Kimi a second challenge: use my AI trading desk to research ideas, build strategies, backtest them and organize the results inside an AI Trading Arena.

This uses the research workflow behind the automated trading setup I used to double my account last year—but this time, Kimi Code is doing the work.

The first live trade lost money. Later, Kimi had 11 positions open. Meanwhile, its research session produced 151 strategy candidates—but some impressive equity curves came with serious drawdowns.

Excessive sugar consumption doesn’t usually cause noticeable problems right away. You could consume a cup of sugar every day for 10 years before experiencing the negative effects of sugar on your health. Discover the sources of hidden sugar in your diet, the consequences of insulin resistance, and how excessive sugar consumption can affect your long-term health.

👉 Download Dr. Berg’s Free Daily Health Routine: https://drbrg.co/4A1mqVY

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

You could consume one cup of sugar every day for 10 years without noticing any obvious problems. Your A1C and blood sugar may still be normal, although you might experience brain fog. The average adult consumes around 50–57 teaspoons of sugar daily.

Much of this sugar comes from hidden sugar in starches, which can have a higher glycemic index than table sugar. Your blood sugar may still appear normal because insulin removes sugar from the blood. Many people have high insulin without knowing it because they never test their fasting insulin. Ideally, you want your fasting insulin below 5.

Chronic health conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol can take 15–20 years to develop after prolonged periods of high insulin and insulin resistance.

Common sources of hidden sugar include:
● Cereal
● Orange juice
● Whole wheat toast
● Baked potatoes
● Pasta
● Low-fat yogurt
● Soda
● Sports drinks

Chronic starch and sugar consumption can lead to insulin resistance, significantly affecting your metabolic health over time. Intermittent fasting and reducing your carbohydrate and sugar intake can help support healthy insulin and blood glucose levels.

DATA:

Weak fades, poor contact, and shots that never feel compressed usually come from the same source: an open club face that forces you to flip the club and swing over the top just to get the ball started at the target. It's one of the most common patterns Eric Cogorno sees in golf lessons, and as with a recent student, the fix starts earlier in the swing than most golfers expect — with the wrist angles that control where the glove logo, right palm, and club face point from takeaway to impact. Get those wrist angles right and you can swing from inside, get your hands ahead of the club head at impact the way Adam Scott's golf swing does, and compress the golf ball for more solid, straighter shots that go farther. The golf tips and golf drills in this lesson also adjust the move for your golf grip, your swing speed, and the club in your hands, so you know how to hit irons and driver with the right amount of shaft lean. If you leave this video without trying the finish line drill, you're leaving solid, compressed iron shots on the table.

✅ How to hit irons and driver with less shaft lean as swing speed drops or clubs get longer

28.10.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

videos.title: Google Genie 4 Is INSANE: AI Can Now Create Worlds You Can Play In!
videos.summary_source_text:
Google Genie 4 Is INSANE: AI Can Now Create Worlds You Can Play In! Google DeepMind just unveiled Genie 4, its most realistic AI world model yet. It generates photorealistic, interactive worlds with real-time audio, changing weather, and AI-controlled characters. But there's a catch: these worlds only stay consistent for about TWO MINUTES.

Announced on October 27, Genie 4 goes far beyond traditional AI video generation. Instead of producing a fixed video, Google's world model lets you step inside an AI-generated environment, explore it using WASD controls, interact with objects, and modify the scene while it's running.

There's no traditional game engine underneath. Every frame is synthesized by AI, with Google's Gemini Omni providing the visual foundation.

And the demonstrations are impressive.

Google showcased a dragon flying at approximately 140 km/h, a jazz saxophonist performing on a floating platform, a hot-air balloon over Antarctica, a crowded 1980s Japanese train station, and an entire stained-glass world.

Even more interesting are the physics demonstrations: flowing satin fabric reacting to wind and a spinning maple seed falling through the air.

But these carefully selected demos raise an important question: How well does Genie 4 handle unpredictable interactions outside Google's controlled examples?

One of Genie 4's biggest upgrades is native audio generation.

Unlike Genie 3, which generated silent worlds, Genie 4 produces environmental sounds, music, and character dialogue alongside its visuals. The dragon demo includes wind and wingbeats, the saxophone performance features synchronized jazz, and characters can even converse in different languages.

However, DeepMind reportedly acknowledges that audio accuracy remains a work in progress.

Then there's the Gemini integration.

Google demonstrated a system where Gemini acts as a director, breaking complex goals into individual instructions, sending them to Genie 4, reviewing the generated results, and adjusting its next actions.

In one example, Gemini guides a simulated Apptronik Apollo humanoid robot through a game of checkers.

This could eventually matter for AI agents, robotics training, and artificial general intelligence (AGI). But it's important to distinguish a simulated robot demonstration from proven real-world robotic capabilities.

The biggest limitation is still world consistency.

After approximately two minutes, Genie 4 can begin losing object permanence. Textures drift, characters may change appearance, and objects don't always remain where they should.

There's also no dedicated physics engine. Genie 4 learns physical behavior from video rather than calculating it through traditional simulations.

And generating readable text inside these worlds remains a challenge.

Google also hasn't released a Genie 4 research paper or model card, and independent researchers haven't yet verified its performance.

So how does it compare with the competition?

Runway's GWM Worlds 2 offers continuous generation at 720p and 24 FPS with 48 kHz audio. Decart's Oasis 3 focuses on robotics applications, while World Labs' Marble creates persistent 3D environments that can be revisited.

Genie 4's potential advantage lies in its claimed photorealism, interactive audio, and integration with Gemini's reasoning capabilities. But without independent head-to-head benchmarks, there's no confirmed winner.

Availability is another limitation.

Genie 4 is currently a restricted research preview, with Google planning access through Project Genie for Google AI Ultra subscribers and selected developers through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

In this video, we examine what Google actually demonstrated, how Genie 4 compares with Genie 1, Genie 2, and Genie 3, what its technical limitations reveal, and whether AI-generated interactive worlds could eventually transform gaming, filmmaking, robotics, and AGI research.

The bigger question isn't whether Genie 4 can generate an impressive world for two minutes.

It's whether Google can make that world persistent, reliable, and physically consistent enough to become genuinely useful.

Is Genie 4 the future of interactive AI, or are we still watching carefully curated technology demos?

Share your thoughts in the comments, and subscribe to BitBiased for independent analysis of AI breakthroughs, emerging technology, and the competition shaping the future.

videos.title: China Just Released a 2.8 TRILLION Parameter AI — Beats GPT-6 Astra!
videos.summary_source_text:
China Just Released a 2.8 TRILLION Parameter AI — Beats GPT-6 Astra! Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro just scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 in independent testing, beating Claude Sonnet 5.5 and recording the highest score Artificial Analysis had measured at publication. Its predecessor, Kimi K3, managed just 13%. That's a massive 54-point improvement without building an entirely new foundation model.

But here's the twist: despite that record-breaking result, Kimi K3.1 Pro ranks only fourth overall on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, behind Claude Opus 5.5 and other frontier models.

So is China's latest AI model genuinely challenging OpenAI and Anthropic, or are the headlines missing something important?

Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3.1 Pro on October 24, 2026, with major improvements in autonomous coding, agentic workflows, long-context reasoning, and tool use. Unlike previous releases focused on scaling model size, K3.1 builds on Kimi K3's existing mixture-of-experts architecture, featuring approximately 2.8 trillion total parameters and 104 billion active parameters.

Independent benchmarks reveal a complicated picture.

Artificial Analysis measured Kimi K3.1 Pro at 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5's 64%. AutomationBench performance jumped from 58% to 73%, while its Intelligence Index increased from 44 to 55.

However, Claude Opus 5.5 still leads overall with an Intelligence Index of 58. Kimi also trails leading competitors in web development and scientific agent tasks.

And Moonshot's own benchmark comparisons require careful interpretation. Different evaluation harnesses, scoring methods, and testing configurations make some headline comparisons less definitive than they appear.

Then there are Kimi's ambitious demonstrations.

Moonshot showcased an AI agent developing a human walking simulator involving 296 skeletal components and 402 muscle components. After 167 missions and 420 reviews, the company says its system achieved 11.2 seconds of alternating stride.

Kimi K3.1 Pro also generates 3D environments using Blender, CAD tools, Three.js, Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot.

But this isn't a native 3D foundation model. Kimi creates 3D content primarily by writing and executing code through existing software tools. And several impressive demonstrations still lack independent reproduction.

The cybersecurity story is even more interesting.

Moonshot disclosed that it deliberately reduced Kimi K3.1 Pro's vulnerability-exploitation capabilities during training.

On its internal xdev-bench-hard benchmark, an unfiltered checkpoint scored 90.5%, while the released model scored 81.0%. The previous Kimi K3 scored just 33.3%.

That means Moonshot reportedly weakened the model's offensive cybersecurity abilities without eliminating them. These results remain independently unverified.

This raises difficult questions about AI safety, open-weight releases, and whether dangerous capabilities can be selectively reduced without affecting legitimate programming skills.

And speaking of open weights, Moonshot has promised to release Kimi K3.1 Pro's weights by November 4, 2026.

If delivered, Artificial Analysis projects it could become the highest-scoring open-weight model on its Intelligence Index, dramatically narrowing the gap with proprietary AI systems.

But until the weights arrive, that remains a promise rather than a completed release.

Pricing adds another dimension.

Kimi K3.1 Pro costs approximately $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens at tracked international rates.

That's roughly 80% cheaper than GPT-6 Astra and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5.

However, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash remains significantly cheaper, and Moonshot's faster Kimi Highspeed option comes at approximately double the cost.

There are also practical concerns about inference speed, reasoning-token consumption, hardware requirements, API reliability, and the rate limits users encountered following launch.

So where does Kimi K3.1 Pro actually stand against GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and DeepSeek?

We examine the independent benchmarks, Moonshot's technical claims, the 3D demonstrations, cybersecurity filtering, open-weight promises, and the real cost of running this model.

Because the biggest story might not be that Kimi beat a frontier model on one benchmark.

It might be what Moonshot achieved without building a bigger foundation model.
